title: Tiered prefix-aware content-hash cache for embedding endpoints (LRU + TTL coherence)
text:
Tiered prefix-aware content-hash cache for embedding endpoints (LRU + TTL coherence)

description:
Problem: Embedding and reranking endpoints are a major driver of per-request cost and p99 latency for short-text workloads. We see repeated requests for similar prefixes (titles, query heads) and near-duplicate content across customers. Current embedding cache is per-object and has limited TTLs and no coordinated invalidation. This ticket proposes a tiered caching scheme that combines prefix-aware caching, content-based hashing for deduplication, and coherence policies (LRU + TTL + versioning) to reduce redundant embedding calls while preserving quality for reranking and similarity search.

acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end integration: new cache layer is enabled behind feature flag for embeddings endpoint and respects existing routing/authorization behavior
2) Latency: 95th percentile embedding endpoint latency reduced by >=15% in canary traffic compared to baseline when cache hit rate >= 40%
3) Cost: API token/compute cost per 1k requests drops by >=12% at steady-state cache hit rate >= 50%
4) Correctness: deduplication false-positive rate (different documents colliding to same cached embedding) < 0.01% measured over sampled corpus
5) Invalidation: content-version invalidation path works end-to-end (content hash change invalidates entry within 5s of upstream publish event), and fallback to recompute is exercised in canary
6) Observability: dashboard shows cache hit/miss, prefix hit breakdown, dedupe rate, and embedding-quality drift compared to non-cached baseline; alerts added for cache hit rate drop > 20% on production traffic

updates:
2025-02-10 — Maya Chen created ticket and attached initial draft design (Confluence link). Identified problem areas from telemetry: high repeat embedding requests for short query prefixes and title-like content.
2025-02-11 — Architecture sync with infra: agreed on a tiered approach: local LRU (per-replica) + regional shared cache (Redis cluster) keyed by content hash + optional prefix index for short text. Chose Murmur3-128 for fast hashing with 128-bit prefix to minimize collisions.
2025-02-12 — Prototype: Diego implemented a micro-prototype that computes content-hash + prefix-key and records hit/miss. Local LRU borrowed from existing request cache abstraction. Benchmarked on 100k queries: naive dedupe cut calls by 37% for synthetic title workload.
2025-02-13 — Security review triage: no new secrets or expanded network access required; Redis cluster already in VPC. Marked security_review_required=false but added audit log requirement for cache invalidation paths.
2025-02-14 — Design review with PM/UX: discussed UX for feature flag and how to expose cache metrics in Console. PM requested an opt-out per-customer label and an admin control to force cache purge for compliance customers.
2025-02-16 — Instrumentation plan added: sample embeddings stored alongside cached metadata for periodic offline quality checks (cosine-sim vs recomputed embedding). Added metric names for instrumentation (embed_cache.hit_rate, embed_cache.prefix_hit_rate, embed_cache.collision_rate, embed_cache.invalidation_latency).
2025-02-17 — Canary rollout plan drafted: start with 1% of traffic from non-enterprise customers for 48h, then 5% for 72h with automated rollback if drift > 0.02 in average similarity for top-k reranking tasks. Diego opened PR (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2381) containing implementation and unit tests.
2025-02-18 — Load test results: under 1k rps synthetic mix, regional shared cache reduces backend embedding compute by 45% and p99 latency improved from 210ms to 170ms on canary. Next: validate on production-sampled traffic and add canary alarms.

decisions:
Use a two-level cache: in-memory LRU per-worker (fast, tiny TTL) + regional Redis cluster as authoritative shared layer.
Primary cache key = SHA256(content) with a short prefix key for title-like inputs (first 64 bytes normalized) to accelerate prefix queries; store metadata: model-version, content-version, timestamp, sample-embedding (float32->quantized bytes).
Use TTL + LRU + explicit version invalidation: default TTL 24h for static content, 10m for short-query prefixes; customers can set 'compliance' flag to force shorter TTL or disable shared caching.
Implement soft-fallback policy: on cache hit with model-version mismatch, return cached embedding only if model-version is compatible (same architecture + quantization), otherwise recompute and update cache.
Detect and record collisions by verifying recomputed embedding similarity on sampled hits; if collision detected, tag entry and move it to a 'pinned' isolated bucket to avoid repeated wrong dedupes.

next_steps:
Finalize Redis key schema and TTLs with infra (Diego + Priya).
Complete integration tests and e2e contract tests for invalidation path (Maya).
Add Console visualization for per-tenant cache hit rate and a manual purge API for enterprise customers (PM: Arun).
Run production-sampled quality evaluation on 50k real queries to measure quality drift before wider rollout.
Prepare rollout runbook and rollback criteria (on-call + SRE input).

comments:
Priya Natarajan (2025-02-11): We should be careful about cache staleness for private deployments. Suggest adding a customer-level metadata key for 'cache_policy' so Private can opt into strict invalidation.
Arun Gupta (2025-02-14): PM asks that we include an admin endpoint in Console to purge on-demand. Also requested per-route metrics to avoid noisy global aggregates.
Sofia Martinez (2025-02-16): During sampling we saw a few collisions on tiny 8-char texts; recommend increasing hash size for short texts or special-casing very short inputs to avoid dedupe at shared cache layer.
Diego Alvarez (2025-02-17): PR opened and tests added. Noted an implementation detail: quantized sample-embedding stored as base64 to keep Redis payload small and deterministic across clients.
